'''Luigi Maria Venanzi''' was an [[inorganic chemist]] who was recognized for diverse contributions to [[coordination chemistry]].  He was born in Italy in 1927.<ref>{{cite web |title=L. M. Venanzi Distinguished Lecture |url=https://chab.ethz.ch/en/research/institutes/LAC/venanzi.html}}</ref>

After receiving his diplom degree at the [[University of Kiel]], he took a position at ICI Laboratories, where he published extensively with [[Joseph Chatt]].  He then proceeded to receive his D.Phil. at Oxford, where he remained as lecturer until 1968.  He left England to become professor at [[SUNY Albany]] and later the [[University of Delaware]].  He then moved to ETH, succeeding [[Gerold Schwarzenbach]].  He finished his career in Switzerland, working extensively on platinum phosphine complexes and [[31P NMR spectroscopy]].<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/s0010-8545(00)00257-5 |title=Transition Metal Hydrides as Ligands |date=2000 |last1=Albinati |first1=Alberto |last2=Venanzi |first2=Luigi M. |journal=Coordination Chemistry Reviews |volume=200-202 |pages=687–715 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/s0020-1693(00)90084-7 |title=<sup>31</sup>P and <sup>195</sup>Pt NMR Studies of the Cluster Complexes &#91;Pt<sub>3</sub>(μ<sub>2</sub>-CO)<sub>3</sub> (Tertiary phosphine)<sub>3</sub>&#93; |date=1981 |last1=Moor |first1=A. |last2=Pregosin |first2=P.S. |last3=Venanzi |first3=L.M. |journal=Inorganica Chimica Acta |volume=48 |pages=153–157 }}</ref>

A lecture award was created in his memory in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=L. M. Venanzi Distinguished Lecture |url=https://chab.ethz.ch/en/research/institutes/LAC/venanzi.html |website=ETH Zurich |access-date=4 September 2024}}</ref>
